Guarding the faith from false teaching
One Scripture, quoted across the groups
Leaders and the life of the church

Paul insists that "a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law", yet that believers are "created ... unto good works"; James that "faith, if it hath not works, is dead"; Hebrews that "without faith it is impossible to please him"; 1 John that "our faith" is "the victory that overcometh the world". Schaff read James's teaching as "no protest against that of Paul, but prior to it"; the James, Peter and Jude page sets out the other readings. Romans 3:28 Galatians 2:16 Ephesians 2:8–10 Titus 3:8 James 2:17 James 2:24 +2 more [5]
Choose a name to see who they were and where they appear.

Thirteen letters open with his name. Outside them, 2 Peter calls him "our beloved brother Paul" and knows "all his epistles". Eusebius counted Hebrews as Paul's fourteenth letter, noting that the church of Rome disputed it; Hebrews itself never names its writer. Romans 1:1 2 Peter 3:15–16 [32]
Every place the letters name, and where.
Ephesians · The words "at Ephesus" are absent from the oldest manuscripts; Tischendorf's Greek text prints them in brackets. Ephesians 1:1
1 John (implied) · Not named in the letter. Early tradition places John at Ephesus late in his life.
2 John (implied) · Not named in the letter. Plummer, Westcott and Easton think it was written from the same place as 1 John.
3 John (implied) · Not named in the letter. Tradition places the elder's letters at Ephesus.
